fullText.simplified:
船和箭

    天黑了，船开过来了，荆州的军队马上对着船放箭。放了一会儿，船就开走了。荆州的军队放心了，回去吃晚饭。刚吃了一会儿，听说船又开过来了，他们马上回到河边，再对着河上的船放箭。过了一会儿，船又开走了。到了晚上，荆州的军队刚准备睡觉，船又回来了，他们又去河边放箭。过了一会儿，船又开走了。
    就这样，河上的船来了走，走了来，每天来来去去有五六次。每次来，荆州的军队都是放箭。虽然大家都觉得奇怪，但心里还是很高兴，很多人都说：“江东人太胆小了，看到我们的箭，就不敢来了。”
    三天过去了。
    第四天，天气变好了。
    船又来了，这一次来的船比前几天都要多。每个人都看得很清楚，那是江东军队的船，船上的人是江东的军队。船开得很快，马上就到了荆州军队面前。
    这么多船，这么多人，还来得这么快！
    刘表急了，大声说：“快放箭！”但是等了很长时间都没有人放箭，他生气地问：“为什么还不放箭？”一个助手着急地跑到他身边，小声说：“没有箭了，这几天我们把箭都放完了。”
    刘表眼睛都大了，他想了想这几天的怪事，终于明白了为什么河上的船总是来了走，走了来。
    江东的船近了，江东的军队杀过来了。他们放着箭、拿着刀，大声说：“杀了刘表！”
fullText.traditional:
船和箭

    天黑了，船開過來了，荊州的軍隊馬上對著船放箭。放了一會兒，船就開走了。荊州的軍隊放心了，回去吃晚飯。剛吃了一會兒，聽說船又開過來了，他們馬上回到河邊，再對著河上的船放箭。過了一會兒，船又開走了。到了晚上，荊州的軍隊剛準備睡覺，船又回來了，他們又去河邊放箭。過了一會兒，船又開走了。
    就這樣，河上的船來了走，走了來，每天來來去去有五六次。每次來，荊州的軍隊都是放箭。雖然大家都覺得奇怪，但心裡還是很高興，很多人都說：“江東人太膽小了，看到我們的箭，就不敢來了。”
    三天過去了。
    第四天，天氣變好了。
    船又來了，這一次來的船比前幾天都要多。每個人都看得很清楚，那是江東軍隊的船，船上的人是江東的軍隊。船開得很快，馬上就到了荊州軍隊面前。
    這麼多船，這麼多人，還來得這麼快！
    劉表急了，大聲說：“快放箭！”但是等了很長時間都沒有人放箭，他生氣地問：“為什麼還不放箭？”一個助手著急地跑到他身邊，小聲說：“沒有箭了，這幾天我們把箭都放完了。”
    劉表眼睛都大了，他想了想這幾天的怪事，終於明白了為什麼河上的船總是來了走，走了來。
    江東的船近了，江東的軍隊殺過來了。他們放著箭、拿著刀，大聲說：“殺了劉表！”

sentences.english: When it got dark, the boats sailed over, and Jingzhou’s army immediately fired arrows at the boats.

sentences.simplified: 放了一会儿，船就开走了。荆州的军队放心了，回去吃晚饭。
sentences.traditional: 放了一會兒，船就開走了。荊州的軍隊放心了，回去吃晚飯。

sentences.traditional: 他們馬上回到河邊，再對著河上的船放箭。
sentences.pinyin: tā men mǎ shàng huí dào hé biān zài duì zhe hé shang de chuán fàng jiàn
sentences.english: They immediately went back to the river and fired arrows at the boats on the river again.

sentences.simplified: 过了一会儿，船又开走了。

sentences.pinyin: guò le yí huì'r chuán yòu kāi zǒu le
sentences.english: After a while, the boats sailed away again.

sentences.simplified: 到了晚上，荆州的军队刚准备睡觉，船又回来了，他们又去河边放箭。
sentences.traditional: 到了晚上，荊州的軍隊剛準備睡覺，船又回來了，他們又去河邊放箭。
sentences.pinyin: dào le wǎn shang jīng zhōu de jūn duì gāng zhǔn bèi shuì jiào chuán yòu huí lái le tā men yòu qù hé biān fàng jiàn
sentences.english: At night, just as Jingzhou’s troops were getting ready to sleep, the boats came back, and they went back to the river to fire arrows.

sentences.simplified: 过了一会儿，船又开走了。
sentences.traditional: 過了一會兒，船又開走了。
sentences.pinyin: guò le yí huì'r chuán yòu kāi zǒu le
sentences.english: After firing for a while, the boats sailed away again.

sentences.traditional: 就這樣，河上的船來了走，走了來，每天來來去去有五六次。

sentences.english: Every time they came, Jingzhou’s troops would fire arrows. Even though everyone thought it was strange, they were still happy.

sentences.traditional: 三天過去了。

sentences.english: On the fourth day, the weather got better.

sentences.simplified: 船又来了，这一次来的船比前几天都要多。
sentences.traditional: 船又來了，這一次來的船比前幾天都要多。

sentences.english: Jiangdong’s boats were near, and Jiangdong’s troops attacked. They fired arrows and held swords, shouting: “Kill Liu Biao!”

sentence_translations: Boats and Arrows
When it got dark, the boats sailed over, and Jingzhou’s army immediately fired arrows at the boats.
After firing for a while, the boats sailed away. Jingzhou’s troops stopped worrying and went back to eat dinner.
After eating for a short while, they heard that the boats had come back.
They immediately went back to the river and fired arrows at the boats on the river again.
After a while, the boats sailed away again.
At night, just as Jingzhou’s troops were getting ready to sleep, the boats came back, and they went back to the river to fire arrows.
After firing for a while, the boats sailed away again.
Just like that, the boats on the river would come and go. Every day they would come and go five or six times.
Every time they came, Jingzhou’s troops would fire arrows. Even though everyone thought it was strange, they were still happy.
Many people said, “People from Jiangdong are too timid. They see our arrows and are too scared to come.”
Three days passed.
On the fourth day, the weather got better.
The boats came again, and this time with more boats than in any of the previous days.
Everyone could see very clearly that these boats belonged to Jiangdong’s army and that the men on the boats were Jiangdong’s troops.
The boats were sailing very fast and quickly arrived in front of Jingzhou’s troops.
So many boats, so many men, and they came so fast!
Liu Biao became anxious and said loudly, “Quick, fire arrows!”
But after waiting a long time, no one had fired any arrows, and he asked angrily, “Why aren’t you firing arrows?”
An assistant ran to him anxiously and said in a quiet voice, “There are no arrows left. We fired them all over the past few days.”
Liu Biao’s eyes widened, and he thought about the strange events of the past few days.
He finally understood why the boats on the river would always come and go.
Jiangdong’s boats were near, and Jiangdong’s troops attacked. They fired arrows and held swords, shouting: “Kill Liu Biao!”
